Incorporating the January 2018 SLOOS alongside the FOMC statement and the FSR lens yields a mildly more constructive read. The FOMC’s macro tone is positive (strong labor market, strengthened outlook, gradual hikes). The SLOOS indicates credit supply to businesses remains accommodative: banks eased or kept unchanged standards and terms for C&I and credit lines, narrowed loan rate spreads, and cited competition/risk tolerance as drivers; some banks also expected to ease standards for small firms and certain mortgages. Offsetting that, pockets of caution are evident: standards tightened for CRE and construction/land development with weaker demand there, consumer credit shows mixed signals with some tighter terms and weaker current demand for credit cards/HELOCs, and banks expect some deterioration in consumer credit performance and a tendency to tighten standards in those categories. Netting these, near‑term credit availability looks supportive of growth, which slightly tempers the FSR caution. Mildly positive overall, nudged up by SLOOS.
